intro: Welcome to Rock, Paper, Scissors versus AI. In the next few minutes, I'll show you how to play, and every feature of the game.
screen: This is the game screen. Your webcam feed is in the middle, and the AI's card sits on the right. The AI plays against you, and tries to learn your habits.
rock: To play, show your move with your hand. A fist is rock. The badge shows what the AI sees, and how confident it is.
paper: An open palm is paper. The skeleton on your hand is what the hand tracker sees.
scissors: And two fingers make scissors. Your hand can be tilted, and at any distance.
nohand: If your hand leaves the frame, the badge tells you.
difficulty: Next, choose a difficulty. Easy plays at random. Medium counters your favourite move. And Hard runs several predictors at once, and trusts whichever reads you best.
start: To start a match, press Start, or the space bar. It's best of five, so the first to win three rounds takes the match.
countdown: Rock, paper, scissors, shoot! The AI locks in its move before the countdown even begins. Show your move right on shoot, and hold it for a moment.
result: The AI's card flips, and the round is scored. The banner explains who won, and the scoreboard keeps track.
proof: But how do you know the AI isn't cheating? Before each countdown, it publishes a hash of its move and a secret. After the round, it reveals both.
verify: Anyone can check it. Run this command, and the output must match the hash that was shown before shoot.
playon: Now let's keep playing. Our test player has a habit: after losing, they always play rock. Watch how quickly Hard mode catches on.
say1: Look at the score. The AI has spotted the pattern, and it keeps answering with paper.
newmatch: A new match keeps everything the AI has learned. Every match adds to what it knows about you.
say2: Humans are bad at being random. The longer you play, the better the AI reads you.
report: When a match ends, you get a report of what the AI learned about you. It only lists habits that are too strong to be luck.
brain: The AI brain panel shows what it was thinking last round: its prediction, which predictor it trusted, and whether it guessed right.
accuracy: Here you can see how well each predictor reads you. The tick mark shows pure chance.
chart: And this chart tracks the AI's win rate over time. Above the gray line, it's beating you more often than luck would.
cheat: Just for fun, there's a cheat mode. The AI peeks at your hand, and always wins.
caught: But look. The reveal doesn't match the commitment, so the fairness proof catches the cheating straight away.
train: You can also train the game on your own hands, in the Train gestures tab. That includes two extra moves: lizard, and Spock.
record: Press record, and move your hand around while it captures samples. Tilt it, turn it, and switch hands.
lizard: Here we record lizard, a sock puppet hand.
spock: And Spock, the Vulcan salute. Recording more angles makes the model more reliable.
trainbtn: Then press train. A small neural network learns your gestures right in your browser, in just a few seconds.
use: Check the accuracy, then press, use this model. You can also download it, or combine samples with friends.
powers: Now your own model powers the game, and it knows lizard and Spock too.
unlocked: With lizard and Spock trained, a new mode unlocks. Every move beats two others, and the rules are listed right here.
five: Play with five moves, just like before. The AI, the brain panel, and the report all adapt.
extras: Finally, the game has sound effects and animations. You can mute the sounds with this button.
outro: That's everything. Try to stay unpredictable, and have fun!
